To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Internet usage of older adults in Germany and South Korean differs from the younger generation in that they have different Internet needs; and (2) the Internet needs of older adults are influenced by cultural factors, and therefore a cross-cultural study is necessary.
the Internet is not a one-size-fits-all solution and that the needs of older people are not the same as those of younger people.
the Internet is a tool that can be used for many different tasks, that the use of the Internet is not limited by age, and that the Internet can be used by elderly people for many different purposes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: Do we need a new Internet for elderly people?
a new approach for the development of a needs-oriented Internet for elderly people, which is based on the needs of elderly users.
developing a new approach for assessing user needs, which can be used for the design of user-friendly and culture-specific Internet services.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Internet needs of elderly people can be described and measured using a culturally sensitive instrument.
the Internet needs of elderly people are different from those of younger users.
the Internet is not a panacea for the elderly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Internet needs of the elderly can be differentiated in terms of their use of the Internet and that the Internet needs for the elderly can be assessed using a questionnaire.
the Internet is not a one-size-fits-all solution.
the Internet usage needs of the elderly are not uniform, but rather depend on a variety of factors, including cultural and social aspects.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the development and validation of a culturally sensitive Internet needs assessment instrument is feasible and that the resulting instrument provides a quantitative and qualitatively differentiated assessment of Internet needs.
a cultural perspective on the design of Internet services for elderly people is necessary.
the development and use of a new Internet is not a viable option for the elderly, but rather a new way of thinking about Internet usage that takes into account their needs and abilities is required.
